title: Local low-rank models for turbulent combustion
summary: The TDB-L-CUR framework combines spatially localized manifolds with CSP-based stiffness mitigation. Adaptive clustering and sampling follow the evolving flow without offline training, reducing the cost of detailed combustion simulations.
alt: DNS and TDB-L-CUR predictions of nitrous oxide mass fraction at five time instants in a three-dimensional turbulent premixed flame.
caption: N₂O mass fraction: DNS (top) and TDB-L-CUR (bottom). Kim et al. (2026), Fig. 8.

title: Differential diffusion and ammonia–hydrogen ignition
summary: Using DNS of NH₃/H₂/N₂–air mixing layers, we investigate how preferential hydrogen diffusion and turbulent mixing compete to shape ignition. A tagged-ammonia approach distinguishes fuel-derived nitrogen and provides a consistent measure of differential diffusion.
alt: Chemical explosive mode and temperature fields at four times in a turbulent ammonia–hydrogen mixing layer.
caption: Chemical explosive mode (top) and temperature (bottom), Reₜ = 400. Oh, Kim et al. (2026), Fig. 15.

title: Accelerating chemistry in OpenFOAM
summary: Extending TDB-L-CUR to operator-splitting reacting flow solvers. The framework integrates stiff chemistry at representative grid points and reconstructs time-averaged reaction rates, bringing adaptive model reduction into an OpenFOAM chemistry library.
alt: Baseline, TDB-L-CUR, and absolute-error fields for NNH on a temperature isosurface in a turbulent flame.
caption: NNH on the T = 1200 K isosurface: baseline, TDB-L-CUR, and absolute error. Manuscript in preparation, Fig. 7.
